_comment: Wild horses on the open grass. Nothing on foot catches one, so they are hunted where the ground closes in - and a foal taken young is worth more than any number of them dead (D111).
name: wild_horse
label: Wild horse

_comment: The horse of the steppe peoples: milked through the summer, eaten when it is old, and worth keeping through a winter that would kill a herd of anything else. A community with horses can hold ground no walking people can reach.
name: horse
label: Horse

_comment: Wild yak, on the cold high ground where nothing else grazes. Slow and heavy, and the one large animal a mountain country carries.
name: wild_yak
label: Wild yak

_comment: The yak a highland people keeps: wool off it twice a year, milk enough for cheese, and it grazes ground where a sheep would find nothing. Everything a mountain community needs comes off one animal because nothing else lives up there.
name: yak
label: Yak
